subject: Privatenet control-channel degradation — rollback/mitigation plan & next steps
messages:
From: Atlas Health Ops <ops@atlashealth.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 16 Aug 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Control-channel errors affecting private deployment (privatenet)

Hi Rishi,

We started seeing intermittent 5xx control-channel errors for our privatenet deployment around 08:45 PDT this morning. The inference nodes remained healthy (CPU/GPU OK) but orchestration commands (scaling, config updates) are sometimes timing out and the web console shows the control connection as "degraded".

Attached is a tar of the agent logs and a short connectivity trace. We tried a soft reconnect on our side (restarting the agent) which temporarily improved things but the degradation returned after ~20 minutes.

Impact: occasional failed model rollouts and an inability to trigger scale-ups for short bursts (we hit it twice during a morning batch). No inference data was exposed; this looks like a control-plane handshake/keepalive issue.

Can you confirm if any upgrades or topology changes were pushed from your side overnight? We have a production window later today and need a mitigation plan.

Thanks,
Samir Patel
Atlas Health — Platform Ops

Attachment: connectivity-trace-20280816.log (text)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Atlas Health Ops <ops@atlashealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 16 Aug 2028 09:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Control-channel errors affecting private deployment (privatenet)

Samir — thanks for the quick signal and the trace. We're pulling in the runtime and control-plane leads now. Initial read: there was a small rollout of a connection-management optimization in the management plane between 02:00–03:00 PDT. No broad customer-facing changes were intended, but we've seen a narrow window of noisy reconnects on a subset of privatenet customers in staging starting this morning.

Immediate plan:
- Aditya and I will collect correlated traces and confirm whether your tenant hit the specific kernel path that regresses keepalive handling.
- If confirmed, we will push a targeted flag rollback to managementplane for affected customers within the hour.
- We'll schedule a short bridge at 10:00 PDT to share findings and the rollback timeline.

Can you confirm a safe 30–45 minute window where you can tolerate brief control-plane restarts? We'll avoid rolling inference workers, only the management plane layer.

— Rishi
VP, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Atlas Health Ops <ops@atlashealth.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 16 Aug 2028 09:54:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Control-channel errors affecting private deployment (privatenet)

Hi all — quick technical summary from correlating traces:
- Root cause signal: regression in the new connect-keepalive batcher that changed timing for stale-KV eviction when node reconnects happen during high-control-plane churn.
- Symptom: management-plane returned ephemeral 503/504 while the eviction/handshake path retried; agents mark connection degraded but keep local inference alive.
- Scope: observed on ~6 customers in staging and 2 production tenants (including Atlas). Likely triggered by a confluence of burst scale events + our micro-optimization.

Mitigation executed:
- I have pushed a targeted rollback flag (managementplane.feature.connect-batcher=false) for Atlas' tenant; the flag flips at 10:05 PDT.
- Please monitor the console after 10:10 PDT for control-channel stabilization; expect transient reconnects up to ~90s as sessions reprovision.

Attachments: rollback-checklist.pdf (short runbook), connectivity-trace-20280816.log (from Atlas).

If the rollback does not stabilize within 15 minutes, plan B is a coordinated management-plane restart; I'll outline the steps on the bridge.

— Aditya
Senior Software Engineer, Runtime

From: Atlas Health Ops <ops@atlashealth.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>

Date: Thu, 16 Aug 2028 10:26:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Control-channel errors affecting private deployment (privatenet)

Rishi/Aditya — thanks, we saw the console mark control-channel stable around 10:12 PDT and our scale-run that previously failed now completes. No further 5xx in the last 20 minutes.

We're still collecting logs on our side but so far the rollback looks successful. Appreciated the rapid response and the runbook — we'll hold on scheduled production changes until you confirm the root cause and next steps.

— Samir
Atlas Health — Platform Ops

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Atlas Health Ops <ops@atlashealth.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 18 Aug 2028 15:41:00 -07:00
Subject: Post-incident summary & follow-ups — control-channel degradation (Aug 16)

Samir — follow-up as promised after our internal RCA work and cross-team review. TL;DR: the management-plane connect-keepalive batcher micro-optimization caused a timing regression when combined with bursty scale events; this led to transient handshake failures and 5xx from the control layer. We rolled back the feature for affected tenants (flag) and validated stabilization.

What we did:
- 2028-08-16T09:05 PDT — customer reported degradation; we triaged and confirmed scope.
- 2028-08-16T10:05 PDT — targeted flag rollback for Atlas tenant applied.
- 2028-08-16T10:12 PDT — control-channel stabilized for Atlas; monitoring validated for 30+ minutes.

Impact: intermittent failed rollouts and brief inability to scale for affected customers; no inference data exposure and no worker-level crashes. Estimated customer downtime for scaling operations: median 45s reconnection time during the window.

Root cause: incorrect eviction timing in keepalive batcher code path introduced in release 2028.07.31 that surfaced under bursty control-plane churn.

Action items / compensation:
- (Infra) Aditya to add deterministic unit tests and chaos harness for keepalive timing by 2028-09-02.
- (Release) Marissa to add a canary gating step for management-plane micro-optimizations for privatenet customers by 2028-09-09.
- (Customer comms) Rishi to share finalized postmortem and evidence with Atlas by 2028-08-21.
- We are offering a one-month credit on control-plane SLA for the impacted window; we'll follow up with account team for details.

Artifacts attached: postmortem-draft-v1.md (internal draft), connectivity-trace-20280816.log, rollback-checklist.pdf.

Please let us know if you'd like a deeper evidence bundle (server logs, packet captures) — we can share via secure transfer. We will send a finalized postmortem after the review cycle and will loop in your security contact for any compliance evidence you require.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
VP, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
